head: 55ce5f770c0b8b6bf68580fdc065c519883f18c0
classification_reasons: The overall change (0002) is a security-authz control touching sdlc.yaml's risk_list item 'auth' end to end, spans a new hook (plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py, 985 lines), hooks.json wiring, plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's sandbox layer, and plugin/ci/run_phase.py's settings rewriting -- a large blast radius by any measure.

spec.md still carries accepted residual gaps (sandbox live-proof deferred to a follow-up PR, eval case 0002 deferred to phase (e), a documented ceiling on what the hook can and cannot close) rather than a fully closed, zero-open-question spec.
Existing tests alone did not cover this code before the change (shell_guard.py is new); coverage comes entirely from tests this same change adds, not pre-existing tests.
attempted: Intent: confirmed this fix round applies exactly the three items review #5469970014 requested (test_hooks.py import placement, dead _absolute_rule_root removal, tautological test_evals.py assertion) and nothing else; cross-checked against evidence/fix-requests.json and evidence/review-findings.json, which name the identical three findings (signatures b5a283b4ec19a447, adcf7a1b9e91cd94, c36c64e4b9cb1c69). No scope drift found.

Spec and plan: verified plan.md was updated in the same commit only where the review told the author to (item 3, test_evals.py reversal) and explicitly left unchanged for item 1 (the review said 'do not change plan.md to match the diff' since plan.md already required the function-local import -- the diff now matches the plan instead). Diff touches only the files plan.md's Files-that-change section lists for this round.

Proof: evidence/test.log, build.log and lint.log (exit 0, '1609 passed', 'All checks passed!') carry a timestamp (2026-10-09T11:08:49Z) that precedes the owner's iteration-cap reset (15:15:47Z) and this round's actual commit, so they are stale with respect to HEAD and do not themselves prove this round's three edits. Because of that gap I verified correctness directly from the current source instead of trusting the log: grepped the full repo for `_absolute_rule_root` (zero remaining references outside historical evidence/markdown files, confirming the dead-code removal is complete and the two test call sites were updated to the equivalent `_posix_root(...)` call); grepped tests/test_hooks.py and confirmed zero module-level `shell_guard` imports and exactly 46 function-local `from hooks import shell_guard` occurrences, matching the claimed count, with the hooks.json wiring test's `timeout == 30` assertion still intact as the review required; confirmed evals/cases/ (under the repo root) actually contains exactly the five folders (0001-protected-path-denied .. 0005-hooks-loaded) the new literal list in test_the_framework_suite_s_cases_load asserts, so the replacement is accurate, not just mechanically plausible.

Blast radius: this round's own diff is narrow -- two test files, one dead-code removal in plugin/ci/run_phase.py, and plan.md's own prose; no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no risk_list item is newly touched by these three edits (the change's overall 'auth' risk acceptance predates this round and is unaffected). The version bumps and OPERATING_MODEL.md edits visible in the cumulative diff were already applied in earlier rounds, not part of this one.

Policies: coding-standards rule 7 (no dead code) is the stated reason for item 2 and is satisfied; rule 4 (tests not weakened) holds -- the test_evals.py change strengthens an assertion (tautological self-comparison replaced by a literal ground truth) rather than weakening it, and the test_hooks.py/test_ci.py edits are mechanical, assertion-preserving refactors.

Tests: checked whether any of the three edits could let a bug pass silently -- they do the opposite (the test_evals.py change makes a previously-tautological assertion meaningful); the import-placement and dead-code changes carry no behavioral assertions to weaken.
